item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Why Potential Reunion with Sonny Gray Makes Sense for Cardinals
item.dc:creator: Curt Bishop; Unknown

item.content:encoded:
Last offseason, the St. Louis Cardinals traded Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Nolan Arenado and Brendan Donovan, stripping their roster of established veteran players. However, that seemed to have lit a spark underneath the young players they have on their roster.
Jordan Walker and JJ Wetherholt have emerged as franchise cornerstones, and though they have cooled off towards the end of the season, there is still a lot to be excited about when concerning the future. The Cardinals also saw Alec Burleson emerge as a star.
Though their starting rotation has been their strength, it could use an addition or two in the offseason. Perhaps a reunion with Sonny Gray could make sense.
Why Sonny Gray reunion would make sense
Gray wasn't quite the ace the Cardinals needed him to be in his two years in St. Louis, but he has been that guy for the Boston Red Sox. In 28 starts, the 36-year-old right-hander is 17-5 with a 2.82 ERA. Though he is older now, he would make sense for the Cardinals because he will likely cost a little less than he did when St. Louis orginally signed him after the 2023 season.
He's also a proven veteran leader that can guide the young pitching staff, and is somebody that can anchor the rotation and get them one step closer to returning to postseason contention, and if they struggle again, he could be a trade candidate at the deadline.
But now might be the right time for the Cardinals to supplement what they have already built from within. They have a strong core in place, and some proven pieces could be what they need to take the next step forward in 2027.
Gray does have a mutual option with Boston for 2027 and has considered retirement, but the mutual option will likely be declined. And if he doesn't retire, perhaps he'll see what the Cardinals have built and be interested in returning to St. Louis.
He is a voice that a lot of the Cardinals' young players are familiar with. He also seemed to enjoy his time in St. Louis despite the team's struggles, and with Kyle Leahy, Quinn Mathews and Michael McGreevy emerging, St. Louis could have an even stronger starting rotation in 2027, especially since the farm system is now loaded with pitching, including top prospect Liam Doyle.
There is a lot to be excited about, and signing Gray could be the first step to getting St. Louis back into contention.
Curt Bishop is a freelance sports writer who graduated from Maryville University of St. Louis with a Bachelor of Arts degree in the field of Communication and currently writes as a contributor for various platforms covering Major League Baseball. Curt’s work includes covering trade and free agency predictions, as well as rumors and news. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding St. Louis Cardinals On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.title: [blogs.fangraphs.com] The Weakest Positions on the Remaining American League Contenders
item.dc:creator: Jay Jaffe

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees had to make do without Aaron Judge for all of June, July and August due to a stress fracture in his right first rib. With the days on the calendar dwindling and the AL East title still in play — which is no longer the case after the Rays clinched on Tuesday night — Judge bypassed a rehab assignment, but once he returned, he played in just seven games before landing back on the injured list due to a right calf strain. Both the slugger and the team took great pains to avoid discussing the injury’s specificity and timeline for recovery until Tuesday, when manager Aaron Boone revealed that Judge has a “moderate grade” strain, received a platelet-poor plasma injection, and isn’t expected to be available for the team’s Wild Card Series rematch against the Red Sox.
While deadline acquisition Heliot Ramos has heated up after a very slow start to his pinstriped career, the Yankees’ right field situation is one of the more glaring potential trouble spots among American League contenders. As the playoffs approach, teams no longer have a chance to upgrade from outside their organizations and instead must make do with the talent on hand. What follows here is a look at the most vulnerable teams at each position — something of a companion to my annual pre-deadline Replacement Level Killers series, with a focus on the teams that still have a chance to make the playoffs. For the AL, that means the Rays, Yankees, and Red Sox — all of whom have clinched spots — plus the Guardians, White Sox, Rangers, and Astros, who are battling for the other two division titles and the third Wild Card spot. I’ve taken the Blue Jays out of consideration, as their Playoff Odds now start with a zero in front of the decimal. While full-season performances play a significant part here, I’m more concerned with who’s worst now, with injuries and adjustments in mind. Each position has a headliner (or two, if it’s a job share), but at several positions, I’ve noted other teams with concerns. A companion National League piece will follow.
Catcher: Kyle Teel and Jake Rogers, White Sox
A Top 100 prospect in both 2024 and ’25, Kyle Teel did a very solid job as a rookie last season, hitting for a 125 wRC+ with 1.9 WAR in just 78 games, but he missed the first two months of this season due to a Grade 2 right hamstring strain and then an LCL sprain in his right knee. His replacements, mainly Edgar Quero (a three-time Top 100 prospect) and Drew Romo, struggled so mightily that they headed the catchers’ section on my Replacement Level Killers list, with Quero optioned to Triple-A Charlotte once Teel returned. While Teel’s defense has been an upgrade, he’s hit just .178/.302/.318 (81 wRC+) with an astronomical 37.3% strikeout rate, up from last year’s 25.9%, and his average exit velocity is just 84.5 mph, down from last year’s 88.3 mph. He recently missed time with a left ankle sprain as well.
Romo was optioned to Charlotte in early September during a shuffle that included both Teel’s return and the arrival of the 31-year-old Jake Rogers via the waiver wire. Rogers, who began the year with the Tigers, was traded to the Orioles in late July, then flipped to the Red Sox in the Adley Rutschman trade on August 3 before being sent on his merry way again within a fortnight. He’s now playing for his fourth team this season and has hit just .161/.276/.287 (62 wRC+). All told, White Sox catchers have combined for a 54 wRC+ and -0.4 WAR, both of which rank 29th in the majors; for as much long-term potential as the 24-year-old Teel and 23-year-old Quero (who has played sparingly since being recalled) may have, they’re less than ideal right now.
It’s worth noting that Rutschman, who was on the injured list due to left wrist inflammation when he was sent to Boston as part of a seven-player blockbuster, has struggled to the point that he’s a concern as well. The 28-year-old switch-hitter was batting a solid .251/.331/.433 (116 wRC+) before being sidelined for three weeks — his third IL stint this season, with shorter ones for left ankle inflammation and a concussion while with Baltimore — but he’s hit just .214/.270/.398 (82 wRC+) in 111 plate appearances since being activated. His strikeout rate has spiked from 14.1% to 21.6%, and his average exit velo has fallen by about two ticks. Backup Connor Wong has hit a similarly light .234/.310/.346 (84 wRC+), albeit with dreadful defense (-10 FRV, -8 DRS, -6.6 FRM). The good news is that Rutschman went 3-for-4 with a pair of doubles on Tuesday night against the Guardians; the bad news is that the Red Sox have other injury concerns in their lineup as well.
First Base: Nathaniel Lowe and David Fry, Guardians
Guardians first basemen made my Killers list due to the light production of their platoon of Kyle Manzardo and Rhys Hoskins. At the deadline, they dealt for Nathaniel Lowe and optioned Manzardo to Triple-A Columbus. A couple of week later, they placed Hoskins on the IL due to lower back inflammation and turned to David Fry, a utilityman who can catch. Alas, after getting a 94 wRC+ from their first basemen prior to the deadline, they’ve managed just a 90 wRC+ since. The lefty-swinging Lowe, who hit a robust .266/.341/.480 (123 wRC+) for the Reds, has dipped to .228/.279/.390 (83 wRC+) while hitting a ton of popups. The righty-swinging Fry has done well in his limited duty at first base, but has hit just .192/.312/.349 (90 wRC+) in 202 plate appearances overall.
Hoskins began a swing progression nearly two weeks ago, but with Columbus’ season having ended, a rehab assignment isn’t an option, which doesn’t bode well for an uptick from his .179/.306/.376 (95 wRC+) line. Manzardo (.215/.306/.378, 95 wRC+) didn’t hit the ball as hard at Columbus as he had either in his previous stops there or in Cleveland, and there hasn’t been any buzz about bringing him back in September or October.
Meanwhile in Boston, Willson Contreras has been the team’s top hitter, batting a potent .276/.387/.518 (152 wRC+) with 27 homers, but he’s been limited to four games this month between a left hamstring strain and a hit-by-pitch induced bruised knuckle on his right hand. Fortunately, he avoided a fracture, and returned to swinging a bat on September 20; the Red Sox hope to get him into the lineup before the end of the regular season, but the situation bears monitoring. Mickey Gasper and Nick Sogard have shared duties during his absence. Both have provided above-average production overall; Gasper had been in a 4-for-32 slump before hitting a pinch-homer — his 10th long ball in 218 plate appearances — against the Guardians on Tuesday night.
Second Base: Jose Altuve, Astros
Jose Altuve may wind up in Cooperstown some day, but Father Time has caught up to the diminutive 36-year-old. He’s batting just .250/.308/.402, which has taken a bite out of both the Astros’ offense and his chances at reaching 3,000 hits; his 99 wRC+ is his lowest full-season mark since 2013, while his .327 xSLG is a 57-point drop from last season and a Statcast-era low. What’s more, his defense has reached its nadir, with both his -10 FRV and -16 DRS rating not only as career worsts but also major league worsts at his position. With Yordan Alvarez entrenched at designated hitter and too valuable to risk in left field — he hasn’t used his glove in a postseason game since 2023 — there’s no place to hide Altuve, but also little likelihood he’ll be benched in favor of backup Nick Allen (.271/.318/.371, 95 wRC+).
On the injury front, keep an eye on the return of the Yankees’ Jazz Chisholm Jr., who was activated between games of Tuesday’s doubleheader against the Rays after missing 12 games due to a sprained right thumb. While his offense has dipped from a 125 wRC+ last year to 100 (.233/.313/.403) this year, Chisholm’s 3.4 WAR ranks third among the team’s position players behind Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger, and his total of 19 home runs ranks second. Backups Anthony Volpe (.244/.321/.335, 88 wRC+) and José Caballero (.236/.293/.373, 86 wRC+) are substantial steps down, but if Chisholm has any lingering issues, one of them may be needed to fill in.
Third Base: Ryan McMahon and Amed Rosario, Yankees
Yankees third basemen have combined for -0.1 WAR, the majors’ third-lowest mark. Lefty-swinging Ryan McMahon bears the bulk of the responsibility for that, hitting just .206/.274/.341 (73 wRC+) while playing solid defense. Righty-swinging Amed Rosario has produced a 100 wRC+ while playing third but has hit just .233/.275/.406 (87 wRC+) overall, and he’s been lousy at the hot corner, with -6 DRS and -6 FRV in just 309.1 innings. The righty-swinging Caballero is at least a better defender than Rosario and about on par offensively, and he’s one of the league’s top base thieves, with 34 steals in 45 attempts. He has also out-produced Rosario against lefties, with an 81 wRC+ to Rosario’s 63 — which could be a factor given that the Red Sox can call upon lefties Ranger Suarez and Payton Tolle to start during the Wild Card Series.
Shortstop: Taylor Walls, Rays
For the third year in a row, the defensive metrics have been very split with regards to Taylor Walls. His 21 DRS leads all shortstops (nobody else has more than 10 DRS), but his -2 FRV ranks 23rd out of 30 with at least 500 innings at the position. Between the latter mark and his dismal .222/.308/.294 (73 wRC+) line, he’s produced just 0.7 WAR. That said, neither Jorge Mateo (.205/.250/.318, 55 wRC+) nor Ben Williamson (.244/.304/.327, 79 wRC+), his occasional fill-ins, hits well enough to merit surpassing Wells on the depth chart.
Left Field: Taylor Trammell and LaMonte Wade Jr., Astros
The Astros’ current 1.3 WAR from their left fielders ranks 17th in the majors, ahead of both the Guardians (1.2) and Red Sox (0.8). But between Steven Kwan’s second-half heater and Roman Anthony’s return from a torn tendon in his right ring finger, both of those teams are now in a better spot than Houston. Taylor Trammell made several Top 100 lists as a prospect — he was as high as no. 12 as a 60-FV on our 2019 list — but he’s now 29 and has netted 0.1 WAR in 273 major league games for four different teams. This year he’s hit .200/.292/.355 (84 wRC+) in a career-high 95 games spread across the three outfield positions, with a 95 wRC+ in 237 plate appearances against righties and a 19 wRC+ (ouch) in 41 plate appearances against lefties.
LaMonte Wade Jr., a reliable contributor for the Giants from 2021–24, bottomed out to a 53 wRC+ last year in a season split between San Francisco and Anaheim. He spent the first few months of this season in the White Sox organization but was released on June 1 so he could sign with the Astros, for whom he’s hit .208/.308/.352 (90 wRC+). He’s been protected from facing many lefties and has seen his playing time dry up otherwise, as he’s been in a slump since mid-August. Meanwhile, righty-swinging Nelson Velázquez hasn’t made a very strong case for himself by hitting .192/.255/.414 (81 wRC+) with a 33.6% strikeout rate in 110 plate appearances split between the Cardinals and Astros. With options like these, you can see why playing Alvarez in left and DHing Altuve starts to make some sense.
Center Field: Daulton Varsho, Astros
The first-half struggles of Jake Meyers, Brice Matthews and Trammell landed the Astros on the Killers center field list, so they quite reasonably dealt for Daulton Varsho on August 3. The 30-year-old flychaser was hitting .243/.307/.375 (91 wRC+), and while his once-elite defense has regressed towards average, a performance like that is still good enough to carry the position. He looked like a decent upgrade for Houston, but while his defense has remained solid enough, he’s hit an anemic .172/.224/.311 (48 wRC+), with his strikeout and walk rates both moving in the wrong direction.
A closer look shows that Varsho has actually been hitting the ball slightly harder since the trade, but all season, he’s been producing popups and cans of corn galore because he’s getting under so many pitches. The real fall-off is relative to last year; his pulled air rate has fallen from 29.5% to 18.5%, while his xSLG has dropped from .464 to .354. As with Altuve and the left field situation, the Astros don’t have great alternatives. Matthews, a 24-year-old rookie, has hit just .201/.255/.332 (64 wRC+), and Meyers sustained a season-ending left kneecap injury at Triple-A Sugar Land last week.
Yet another injury-related note for the Red Sox: Ceddanne Rafaela was sidelined nearly three weeks ago due to a right quad strain. Prior to that, he was putting the finishing touches on a breakout season, having hit .282/.317/.443 (108 wRC+) with 16 homers and 17 steals while playing Gold Glove-caliber defense in center field. Less than a week after he went down, his capable fill-in Eli White suffered a ligament injury in his right foot, requiring season-ending surgery. Since then, Jarren Duran and Nate Eaton have shared the position. Rafaela has yet to return to the roster, though manager Chad Tracy said he’s “getting close.” If he does suffer a setback, continuing to play Duran during what’s been an awful season (.204/.261/.362, 68 wRC+) would obviously be less than ideal.
The Yankees’ Trent Grisham was sidelined by a Grade 2 strain of his right hamstring around the same time that Rafaela went down, and he has yet to return as well. His performance has fallen off drastically after a career year; he’s hit just .211/.308/.395 (98 wRC+) with 18 homers while trading some power for contact, and his defense has also been rough (-5 FRV and -8 DRS in 961.1 innings). While Boone has said he could be “in play at some point” during the postseason, there’s little urgency. Rookie Spencer Jones has shifted over from right field and done an impressive job of holding down the fort, playing adequate defense while hitting .246/.316/.435 (110 wRC+) despite a 36.2% strikeout rate.
Right Field: Heliot Ramos and Aaron Judge, Yankees
Yes, that looks weird in print, but for the moment at least, it’s a reality for the Yankees. The 27-year-old Ramos hit a modest .264/.304/.424 (100 wRC+) with nine homers and 0.6 WAR for the Giants before being traded to the Yankees on August 3. He began his time in pinstripes by going 5-for-47, and at one point went 32 games between homers — from July 20 to August 29 — while slugging .204. He’s heated up since then, but his .168/.294/.356 (85 wRC+) line with the Yankees doesn’t give anyone much confidence he can replace even the banged-up version of Judge the Yankees have received in his 66 games this season (.241/.360/.511, 141 wRC+).
In terms of concerns about sheer replacement-level production, the White Sox stand out here. Early in the season, the team tried Everson Pereira, Jarred Kelenic, and Rikuu Nishida as their regular at the position, but none got the job done. On June 9 they called up Braden Montgomery, a switch-hitting 23-year-old who placed 100th on our Top 100 as a 50-FV prospect in the spring. He collected two hits in his debut that night against the Braves, capped by a walk-off homer, but it’s been mostly downhill since then, as he’s hit .212/.305/.340 (84 wRC+) with six homers and 0.5 WAR in 88 games. While he’s hit .248/.344/.385 (110 wRC+) in 250 plate appearances against righties, he’s flailed away at a .125/.204/.2227 clip in 98 plate appearances against lefties. With resurgent lefty-masher Randal Grichuk on the roster and hitting .331/.372/.650 (182 wRC+) in 172 plate appearances against lefties, there’s no reason that should be happening.
Designated Hitter: Andrew Benintendi, White Sox
No remaining AL contender ranks below 15th in the majors in wRC+ provided by their DHs, and the two lowest teams from among that subset, the Red Sox and Guardians, are respectively third and fourth in second-half wRC+ from that spot while using revolving casts of players. So I’m picking (on) Andrew Benintendi, who has hit a very modest .243/.302/.414 (98 wRC+) while starting at DH in 105 games, with Grichuk (19) the only other Chicago player in double digits. There’s nothing particularly terrible or mysterious about Benintendi’s performance, which beyond a September slump, has lined up with his expected stats quite well; he’s got 21st-percentile bat speed but a 66th-percentile squared-up rate and a 77th-percentile hard-hit rate. He doesn’t hit lefties (.227/.261/.250, 44 wRC+ in 47 PA this year), so manager Will Venable has either used Grichuk or one of his righty regulars there. For as impressive as the White Sox’s turnaround from three straight 100-loss seasons has been, you can see from this roundup that the team’s weaknesses have come to the fore as they’ve tried to sew up a playoff berth.
Brooklyn-based Jay Jaffe is a senior writer for FanGraphs, the author of The Cooperstown Casebook (Thomas Dunne Books, 2017) and the creator of the JAWS (Jaffe WAR Score) metric for Hall of Fame analysis. He founded the Futility Infielder website (2001), was a columnist for Baseball Prospectus (2005-2012) and a contributing writer for Sports Illustrated (2012-2018). He has been a recurring guest on MLB Network and a member of the BBWAA since 2011, and a Hall of Fame voter since 2021. Follow him on BlueSky @jayjaffe.bsky.social.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 18:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: David Butler II)
The Boston Red Sox hope to shift some momentum in advance of the playoffs when they host the Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday night in the second game of a three-game series.
Cleveland extended its winning streak to six games by beating Boston 3-2 on Tuesday. It was the third straight loss for the Red Sox (84-73), who have dropped eight of their last 12 games and own a 9-10 record in September but still clinched a wild-card berth on Sunday.Add left-handed reliever Erik Miller to the list of Boston's concerns as the Red Sox prepare for the playoffs. Miller looked sharp when the Red Sox acquired him from San Francisco in August, but he has allowed nine walks and hit two batters in September.One of those hit batsmen scored the game-winning run Tuesday. Miller hit Chase DeLauter to start the ninth inning, and DeLauter ended up breaking a 2-2 tie when he scored on Nathaniel Lowe's sacrifice fly.Miller has given up six runs and six walks in his past 3 1/3 innings and took the loss on Tuesday.'He's working through stuff,' Boston manager Chad Tracy said. 'I thought today was another step in the right direction. The hit batter ... the free passes are what gets you, and I think he also got some bad batted ball (luck). ... We're gonna try to get him out there a couple more times this week. Obviously still trust the stuff. If we can get that right, trust the stuff and his ability to strike out guys.'
Tuesday's win allowed the Guardians (82-75) to remain one game ahead of the Chicago White Sox at the top of the American League Central standings. Chicago has the division tiebreaker over Cleveland, which has a magic number of two to clinch a playoff berth.
Meanwhile, Guardians manager Stephen Vogt called Lowe 'a professional hitter.'
'You know he's not trying to do too much,' Vogt said. 'He's not going up there trying to be a hero, hitting a three-run homer. Just score the guy from third. Got a pitch up in the zone, and was able to drive it deep enough to left. And you know he continues to just make plays for us.'The Guardians won despite stranding 15 runners and a 1-for-12 hitting performance with runners in scoring position.'Again, felt like it was another night where we get a ton of traffic, we put a lot of pressure on, and just weren't able to get the big hit,' Vogt said. 'You know, we were able to get a couple runs across, but we left a lot on the table. But I just love the way we're making guys work. We're getting on base ... and we're going to come through a lot more often than not. And again, our pitching just picked us up again tonight.'Tracy said he expects center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela (quadriceps) to be activated from the injured list on Wednesday. The manager also said first baseman Willson Contreras still has some soreness in his hand and won't be in the lineup Wednesday but is close to returning.Right-hander Sonny Gray (17-5, 2.82 ERA) will start for the Red Sox on Wednesday. He's 8-5 with a 3.12 ERA in 21 career starts against the Guardians. On May 30, he gave up one run on four hits and three walks over six innings against them. He struck out seven in a 9-1 win.Left-hander Foster Griffin (15-5, 3.67 ERA) will start for Cleveland on Wednesday. It will be his first career appearance against the Red Sox.--Field Level Media

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox need Ceddanne Rafaela’s return to be immediate solution to slumping offense
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: No matter what happens for the rest of the season, the Boston Red Sox are a playoff team — they've popped the bottles and showered in the beer that secures their fate. item.content:encoded:
No matter what happens for the rest of the season, the Boston Red Sox are a playoff team — they've popped the bottles and showered in the beer that secures their fate. But Boston's offense hasn't given fans anything to be excited about over the last few games.
The Red Sox have lost eight of their last 12 games and three of their last four series, including one to the MLB-worst Los Angeles Angels. Boston has the second-lowest batting average in September (.221) and the sixth-lowest team OPS (.675). It has just a .179 average with runners in scoring position this month. The Red Sox haven't scored more than four runs since their September 12 game against the Kansas City Royals.
Offensive production that minimal won't keep the Sox alive very long in the postseason. Boston will face the New York Yankees in a Wild Card rematch of last season's series, which didn't end well for a highly-injured, slumping team kind of like this year's squad.
Thankfully, offensive reinforcements are coming, starting with Ceddanne Rafaela. The outfielder has been on the 10-day injured list with a strained hamstring since September 3. Red Sox manager Chad Tracy announced following their September 22 loss that Rafaela would be activated the following day.
Red Sox need Ceddanne Rafaela back to help awaken slumping offense
Rafaela has been one of the most important pieces of Boston's offense all year thanks to the best season of his young career. He's slashing .282/.317/.443 with 32 doubles (tied for the 13th-most in MLB), three triples, 16 home runs and 70 RBI over 135 games.
Rafaela isn't the only missing piece of the Sox's offense, as Willson Contreras is also out of commission after taking a pitch to the side of his hand on September 17. Boston's home run leader never went on the IL so he doesn't have to be formally activated to return to action. He's swung a bat and is on the road to recovery, but the Red Sox haven't announced an estimated return date for him.
Rafaela and Contreras being injured can't be an excuse for the Red Sox's offense disappearing with just days to go in the regular season. They could be playing down since the rest of their games don't technically matter, but the sudden decrease in offensive production is concerning nonetheless.
It serves the Red Sox to go into the playoffs confident and with a humming offense. Rafaela's return could help them get there. but the rest of the bats need to step up, as well.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox haven't been playing their best overall baseball over the last few weeks in the lead-up to the postseason. Arguably, the biggest reason for this is the fact that they have been navigating a few difficult injuries.
For example, center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela hasn't played in a game since Sep. 2 due to a right quadriceps strain. That is expected to change on Wednesday. After the Red Sox's loss against the Cleveland Guardians on Tuesday, Boston manager Chad Tracy shared that Rafaela is expected to be activated off the Injured List on Wednesday and that Willson Contreras has been taking batting practice, as shared on X by The Athletic's Jen McCaffrey.
The Red Sox Are Going To Get A Boost
"Chad Tracy expects Ceddanne Rafaela to be back in the lineup tomorrow. Willson Contreras took BP but still day to day," McCaffrey wrote on X.
Before Rafaela landed on the Injured List, he was smack dab in the middle of the best season of his career to this point. On top of playing Gold Glove Award-level defense in center field, Rafaela was slashing .282/.317/.443 with a .760 OPS, 16 homers, 70 RBIs, 17 stolen bases, 32 doubles and three triples in 135 games played. Rafaela's return shouldn't be understated. This is big news for the Red Sox.
Rafaela has racked up 5.4 wins above replacement this season, which is a new career high. Rafaela has the second-highest total on the Red Sox's roster and is tied for 22nd in baseball in general. If he didn't miss almost a month of action, he'd be much higher as well.
With Rafaela back in the mix, they can slot him in comfortably in center field and near the top of the lineup. With him in center field over guys like Jarren Duran and Nate Eaton. Duran has gotten a chunk of time there since Rafaela got hurt. With center field now full, then it's going to be a question each night whether Boston wants to roll with Duran in left field and Roman Anthony as the DH, or Anthony in left field and then make a decision at DH.
The outfield logjam situation was something that hung over the Red Sox to begin the season. Now, it's a bit different. If the Red Sox were to stick Anthony in left field, there's a good chance that it wouldn't be Duran as the DH. He has shown very solid pop this season, but with five games left, he's batting .204.
Instead, the Red Sox could slide someone, like Mickey Gasper, into the spot. Gasper specifically is batting .259 and bashed his 10th homer of the season on Tuesday. With Rafaela back, Boston's lineup overall can be better. The offense has taken a hit recently, Rafaela is the guy who is going to boost it. Rafaela is going to help himself, and his return could get a struggling bat out of the lineup on a nightly basis. Two positives.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding Boston Red Sox On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.dc:creator: Ian Browne
item.description: BOSTON -- When Payton Tolle walked off the mound with two outs in the top of the sixth inning on Tuesday night, it was the perfect opportunity for the Fenway faithful to recognize the power lefty for an outstanding rookie season. Next time Tolle pitches, the noise is likely to be even louder, and not nearly as favorable. item.content:encoded:
BOSTON -- When Payton Tolle walked off the mound with two outs in the top of the sixth inning on Tuesday night, it was the perfect opportunity for the Fenway faithful to recognize the power lefty for an outstanding rookie season.
Next time Tolle pitches, the noise is likely to be even louder, and not nearly as favorable.
The Red Sox will have no hesitation sending out the confident, charismatic 23-year-old into enemy territory.
While this was far from the best (5 2/3 innings, 8 hits, 2 ER, 2 BBs, 5 K’s) of Tolle’s 26 regular-season starts, it was more than enough to keep the Red Sox in the game.
Assuming Tolle doesn’t pitch again in the regular season, his final stat line includes this: A 3.03 ERA, 171 strikeouts, 40 walks, 1.10 WHIP and a .222 opponents batting average.
Playing short-handed without Willson Contreras (bruised knuckle, right hand), Ceddanne Rafaela (right quadriceps strain, 10-day IL) and Trevor Story (rest), the Red Sox continued their recent trend of not scoring much.
There were two bright spots.
Mickey Gasper came up as a pinch-hitter and hammered a game-tying solo shot to right in the bottom of the eighth.
Adley Rutschman, who had been slumping of late, belted two doubles as part of a three-hit night.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox Injury Update: Aggressive Willson Contreras, Ceddanne Rafaela, Curtis Mead, pitching options
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: Alongside the news that beloved interim skipper Chad Tracy will drop his interim tag, the Boston Red Sox got a slew of positive injury updates. Boston is just six games from the postseason and it needs all the reinforcements it can get. One of the best, if not the best update is that Willson Contreras is swinging a bat following a scary hit by pitch against the Texas Rangers. item.content:encoded:
Alongside the news that beloved interim skipper Chad Tracy will drop his interim tag, the Boston Red Sox got a slew of positive injury updates. Boston is just six games from the postseason and it needs all the reinforcements it can get.
One of the best, if not the best update is that Willson Contreras is swinging a bat following a scary hit by pitch against the Texas Rangers. Contreras on September 17 took a pitch on the side of his hand, immediately fell to the ground in pain and left the game without delay.
Contreras doesn't easily leave games after being plunked, which has happened 24 times this season. His immediate departure led fans to believe he could've been severely injured. Thankfully, that was not the case, as his imaging came back clean. He believed he fractured his hand because it was numb for a few minutes after the hit, but Contreras avoided the worst.
The Red Sox have not announced an estimated return date for Contreras, but any progress is a good sign. He's been Boston's best hitter all season and leads the team in home runs — the Sox can't afford to go to the postseason without him, especially with the New York Yankees' fearsome rotation ahead in the Wild Card series.
Willson Contreras and Ceddanne Rafaela near returns to Red Sox after both take batting practice on September 22
Ceddanne Rafaela also took batting practice on September 22. He hit off Garrett Crochet, who threw 16 pitches before Contreras' turn in the batter's box. The outfielder on September 19 told Alex Speier of The Boston Globe that he hopes to be active for the final homestand of the season, which has already started.
Like Contreras, Rafaela has been one of Boston's most consistent hitters all year. The Soxs offense has faltered without the two in the lineup. If his timeline holds, Rafaela should be back before the postseason so the Red Sox can take full advantage of his clutch timing in huge moments.
Rumors swirl about Curtis Mead's recovery following Garrett Crochet's BP session
There were also rumors that Curtis Mead was expected to hit off Crochet following Rafaela's practice, but there has been no confirmation that he actually swung a bat. The Red Sox acquired Mead from the Washington Nationals at the trade deadline to bring a righty power bat to their lineup, but he was plunked in his second Red Sox at-bat and the pitch fractured his wrist.
The most recent update on Mead from mid-September was that he was still feeling soreness in his wrist when he tried to swing. The soreness would need to subside for his hitting progression to start, and given the time of the season, many people assumed his year had reached its end. Given that he may not have hit against Crochet, it might still be.
Red Sox send Tanner Houck and Johan Oviedo to Fort Myers to stay loose in case of postseason use
Alongside Crochet, the Red Sox have starters-turned-relievers Tanner Houck and Johan Oviedo nearing the end of their respective recoveries. Both pitchers made rehab assignments with the Triple-A Worcester Red Sox before their season ended and they've been sent to Fort Myers to stay loose just in case Boston needs them in the playoffs, according to Chris Cotillo of MassLive.
The Red Sox will have no shortage of pitching depth entering the playoffs, but whether they use any of their rehabbing pitchers is still yet to be seen. Well-rested arms would be helpful, but the team could be concerned about upsetting the chemistry of the preexisting bullpen, which has been one of the best in the sport all year.

item.dc:creator: Scott Roche
item.description: After an off day on Monday, the Boston Red Sox will return to Fenway Park to begin the next-to-last series of the regular season before the playoffs next week. Boston clinched their spot in the postseason after the Atlanta Braves completed a three-game sweep of the Houston Astros on Sunday afternoon. item.content:encoded:
After an off day on Monday, the Boston Red Sox will return to Fenway Park to begin the next-to-last series of the regular season before the playoffs next week. Boston clinched their spot in the postseason after the Atlanta Braves completed a three-game sweep of the Houston Astros on Sunday afternoon.
The Red Sox are all but locked into the second American League wild-card spot. They are on a collision course with the New York Yankees next week in the Bronx for a best-of-three series. Before then, however, Boston has three games with the Cleveland Guardians. They will then host the Chicago Cubs this weekend, weather permitting.
As for the Guardians series, Wilyer Abreu is back in the lineup for manager Chad Tracy and batting in a familiar spot.
Boston Red Sox Announce Wilyer Abreu Spot in Lineup Against Guardians on Tuesday Night
Tracy will send left-hander Payton Tolle to the mound to open the series and as far as his lineup goes, Abreu us back and batting cleanup. Here is Boston's lineup for the series opener against Cleveland's Parker Messick,
Nick Sogard 1B
Jahmai Jones DH
Wilyer Abreu RF
Caleb Durbin 3B
Isiah Kiner-Falefa SS
Nate Eaton CF
Abreu will be batting fourth, with first baseman Willson Contreras still out of the lineup after getting hit by a pitch last Thursday night against the Texas Rangers. He missed the series against the Tampa Bay Rays. As for Abreu, he did not play in Sunday's series finale, a 5-1 loss.
Boston Red Sox Playing Out the String Ahead of Playoffs
Tuesday, it was announced that Tracy was having the interim tag removed, and Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow is having his option in 2029 and 2030 picked up by the club. It's not surprising that it was announced before the playoffs.
Boston is scheduled to send their three projected starters on the mound next week against the Yankees: Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suárez against the Guardians. However, Cleveland is in a heated race with the Chicago White Sox for the American League Central Division title. They enter the series with a one-game lead over the White Sox, who are playing the Kansas City Royals this week.
Boston has slumped in September. However, they can use the six games before next week as a tune-up. As for this weekend, the weather is projected to be a mess. Tim Healy of the Boston Globe reported that MLB has no plans to move the series out of Boston. There are going to be very few windows to play baseball this weekend.
The Cubs are in a battle for home-field advantage in the National League wild-card round. Those games will have big meaning for them and the NL. They enter play this week tied with the San Diego Padres for home-field advantage next week. The Philadelphia Phillies are a game behind. There is a lot riding on this weekend.

item.title: [bosoxinjection.com] Red Sox might've cemented Craig Breslow’s rise off the hot seat too soon
item.dc:creator: Brian Burrows
item.description: The Craig Breslow era in Boston has felt like a roller coaster ride. Hired at the start of the 2023-24 offseason, the Boston Red Sox have not had a losing season under Breslow, despite wild swings in the team's form over the three years. With the Red Sox clinching a playoff berth for the second year in a row, team ownership decided that now was the time to exercise two options on their Chief Baseball Officer's contract, guaranteeing his deal for the 2029 and 2030 seasons. item.content:encoded:
The Craig Breslow era in Boston has felt like a roller coaster ride. Hired at the start of the 2023-24 offseason, the Boston Red Sox have not had a losing season under Breslow, despite wild swings in the team's form over the three years.
With the Red Sox clinching a playoff berth for the second year in a row, team ownership decided that now was the time to exercise two options on their Chief Baseball Officer's contract, guaranteeing his deal for the 2029 and 2030 seasons. On the surface, a head of baseball operations who got his team to the playoffs in years two and three of their time running the club getting years added to their contract, would make sense, but in Breslow's case it isn't as straightforward.
It was only three months ago when most of Red Sox Nation was calling for Breslow's head. The Red Sox were 32-46 on June 24, dead last in the division, and it already seemed like the season was over. It took a miraculous turnaround to get the team to the playoffs. Not to say that Breslow had nothing to do with that; he had added a lot of players to the roster who were key contributors, but that has a lot more to do with the players and coaches than the front office.
Breslow's tenure has also been marred by controversy, specifically the Rafael Devers drama. It was his handling of the situation, along with former manager Alex Cora, that ultimately led to the fracture of the relationship with the team's then-face of the franchise. While the fanbase was split on whose side they took, player or team, his actions after the fact didn't make it any better.
Red Sox's Craig Breslow had the hottest seat of any GM only three months ago
It was the signing of Alex Bregman that caused the Devers drama in the first place. While Breslow was praised for the signing, Bregman opted out at the end of the year and was then not re-signed. The Red Sox went from two elite third basemen to none in the span of a season. It wasn't a good look for the Red Sox CBO.
Now, Breslow's pivot from all of the drama and mess surrounding Devers and Bregman looks incredibly good in hindsight. The additions of Ranger Suarez, Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Caleb Durbin, and others have been extremely impactful to the Red Sox's success this season. While some of those moves were celebrated at the time they happened, others like the Durbin-Kyle Harrison swap (that also netted the Red Sox Andruw Monasterio and Anthony Seigler) were heavily scrutinized.
Breslow also made good moves at the trade deadline, adding Erik Miller and Eli White, who have looked good for the Sox. He also made the splash trade for Adley Rutschman, which hasn't worked as well on the field, but certainly instilled confidence in the team, knowing the front office believed in them.
Red Sox could've softened the impact by extending one of Craig Breslow's options at first
All of this is to say that Breslow's time as CBO hasn't been as smooth sailing as the records would suggest. He has had some high highs but also some low lows. Why did ownership feel the need to exercise both options right now? The first option wasn't needed until the 2029 season, two years out. The second was for 2030, three years out.
Doing the first one now would've been fine — picking up the 2029 option gives Breslow another three comfortable seasons on his contract. That would make him more comfortable making moves for the future and give him the job security to know he will likely be in place to see them play out. Selecting the 2030 option on the same day was unnecessary, though.
There have been too many hiccups in the three years under Breslow to say he has warranted another four seasons. The start of 2026 could easily repeat itself in 2027. Should ownership feel the need to relieve him of his duties early, then this makes it that much harder. Breslow hasn't won a World Series in Boston; in fact, he hasn't even made it out of the Wild Card round. Exercising the option for 2030 feels very premature.
Breslow has not done a bad job in Boston. At the end of the day, it's results that matter, and Breslow's teams have made the playoffs two out of three times. He shouldn't be fearing for his job, but his contract also wasn't ending for another two seasons. It feels early to be handing him the keys so far down the road after the drama of his first two years as CBO.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have been without Willson Contreras since Thursday, when he was hit in the hand by a pitch.
Contreras was not placed on the injured list and is trying to make a return before the end of the regular season. According to manager Chad Tracy, Contreras is "doing much better" and took some swings on Wednesday.
"He was able to swing pretty aggressively in the cage again today," Tracy told MassLive's Christopher Smith.
Contreras was an All-Star this year and is a huge reason why the Red Sox turned their season around. At 34 years old, he is having a career year, hitting .276 with a .905 OPS. If the season ended today, he would tie his career-high batting average and set a new career-high in OPS. He also has a career-high 27 home runs and 81 RBIs.
The Red Sox will need him back in the lineup if they want to make a deep run, but there is no real reason to rush him back in the regular season. The Red Sox are pretty much locked into the No. 5 seed, and the only real benefit of bringing Contreras back for the regular season is to get him a few at-bats before the postseason.
The Red Sox will likely play the New York Yankees in the Wild Card Series. This season, Contreras has just a .673 OPS against the Yankees in 13 games. He will hope to get better results in the postseason, but that won't be easy if his hand is not 100%.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Red Sox ace encouraged after facing live hitters: ‘I could go get outs’
item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo
item.description: Garrett Crochet reached an important milestone in his road to recovery on Tuesday, facing live hitters on the mound at Fenway Park for the first time since his ill-fated comeback attempt in late May. Throwing live batting practice against Ceddanne Rafaela, the Red Sox ace threw 16 pitches, one more than originally planned because he spiked a changeup into the dirt on what was supposed to be his final pitch. The left-hander said he was able to ramp up his intensity to a level he hadn’t reached ye
item.content:encoded:
Garrett Crochet reached an important milestone in his road to recovery on Tuesday, facing live hitters on the mound at Fenway Park for the first time since his ill-fated comeback attempt in late May.
Throwing live batting practice against Ceddanne Rafaela, the Red Sox ace threw 16 pitches, one more than originally planned because he spiked a changeup into the dirt on what was supposed to be his final pitch. The left-hander said he was able to ramp up his intensity to a level he hadn’t reached yet, that his fastball was in the 94-96 mph range, and that following the session he got good feedback from Rafaela.
With that crucial box checked, could Crochet’s next time on the mound come in a game setting? Crochet said it’s too soon to say, but he’s cautiously optimistic about his ability to do so.
“You don’t know until you know I suppose. I would say the way that live just went that I could go get outs,” Crochet said. “It depends, obviously, what role they want me in, like I said it’s not really for me to say, I know myself and I know my body, and the biggest thing is that I felt good out there.”
Crochet has missed the majority of the season due to left shoulder inflammation, which landed him on the injured list in late April after only six starts. What was originally believed to be a short-term injury wound up sidelining Crochet for five months and counting, but after Tuesday’s session there remains a possibility Crochet could factor into the postseason equation for the Red Sox out of the bullpen.
That will be up to chief baseball officer Craig Breslow and manager Chad Tracy, Crochet was sure to emphasize.
“This team has had a great year, I think for me to take a spot on the roster then someone would have to lose one, and I would feel bad doing that because this team has pitched their (butts) off the whole season,” Crochet said. “Ultimately that’s going to be something that’s up to the front office and whenever they gauge that I’m ready then I’ll accept that, and in the meantime I’m just going to keep working my butt off.”
Tracy said he was encouraged by Crochet’s outing, noting that his velocity is climbing and the spin on his pitches looked sharp. The next step will be seeing how his body recovers in the upcoming days and mapping out a plan for the weekend.
“What that looks like now, I don’t know,” Tracy said. “I just know that whatever it is it’s going to be done with Garrett’s best interest in mind.”
Typically the next stage in a throwing progression after throwing live batting practice would be to start a rehab assignment, but given that the minor league season ended this past weekend, that isn’t an option for Crochet. Time also isn’t on the left-hander’s side, so if Crochet is going to pitch in a game before the playoffs, he would have to be activated at some point over the final homestand.
Tracy said those are all factors the club is considering, and while he believes Crochet would be up for the challenge of jumping right into a playoff series, they have to be realistic about where he’s at when it comes time to decide who will be on the playoff roster.
“Knowing the player, if he was healthy and we felt he could he’d probably be like ‘I’m not going to be afraid of that,'” Tracy said. “That being said, we have to consider it and just be very mindful of what are we potentially exposing him to and what can he give us, really? Understanding you don’t want to leave yourself short, so for me it’s been step by step, the next step would be sometime this weekend, let’s see what that entails, and we’ll go from there.”
Rafaela, Contreras getting close
Ceddanne Rafaela (right quad strain) and Willson Contreras (bruised right hand) remain sidelined with their respective injuries, but Tracy said both are getting close to a return.
“(Rafaela) is doing much better, we’re getting close there, and Willson’s also doing much better, he was able to swing pretty aggressively in the cage again today,” Tracy said, adding that Rafaela was scheduled to run and Contreras was set to take batting practice on the field. “(We’ll) let them get through their whole day, see where they’re at and assess, but I think we’re getting pretty close with both of them.”
Staying ready
With the minor league season finished the Red Sox have sent a contingent of players who may potentially factor into the club’s plans the rest of the way to Fort Myers so they can stay ready in the event they’re needed.
Tracy did not have the full list of players available when asked Tuesday, but some of those headed to Fort Myers include pitchers Tanner Houck, Johan Oviedo, Jedixson Paez, Tyler Samaniego and Wyatt Olds, infielders Romy Gonzalez, Franklin Arias and Tsung-Che Cheng, and outfielder Braiden Ward.
Veteran catcher Tomas Nido has also come up from Worcester to serve as an extra catcher on the taxi squad for the Red Sox.
Extra innings
The Red Sox announced Eli White underwent successful Lisfranc repair surgery on his right foot Tuesday. The procedure was performed by Dr. Martin O’Malley at the Hospital for Special Surgery in New York City. … Aroldis Chapman (lat tightness) is feeling much better but is still a day or two away from a return to the mound. … Curtis Mead (fractured left wrist) has resumed swinging a regular bat and is taking overhand batting practice, but while the Red Sox haven’t ruled out a possible return, Tracy acknowledged that time isn’t on his side.

item.title: [NBC Sports Boston] Garrett Crochet says he's ready to 'get outs' for Red Sox
item.dc:creator: Michael Hurley
item.description: Once again, Garrett Crochet donned a full Red Sox uniform, made the walk from the bullpen to the mound, and pitched at Fenway Park on Tuesday afternoon. This time, he faced a live hitter -- in the form of Ceddanne Rafaela -- as he took another step toward returning to the mound for Boston. item.content:encoded:
Once again, Garrett Crochet donned a full Red Sox uniform, made the walk from the bullpen to the mound, and pitched at Fenway Park on Tuesday afternoon. This time, he faced a live hitter -- in the form of Ceddanne Rafaela -- as he took another step toward returning to the mound for Boston.
And for the first time in what's been a long recovery period, the 27-year-old said he feels ready to contribute.
"I would say, the way that that live [batting practice] just went, that I could go get outs," Crochet told reporters inside the Red Sox clubhouse.
That being said, Crochet shared that he has some hesitance to joining the roster, though it has nothing to do with his own health.
"This team's had a great year. I think that for me to take a spot on the roster, then someone would have to lose one. And I would feel bad doing that, because this team has pitched their ass off the whole season," Crochet said. "Ultimately, that's something that's gonna be up to the front office. And whenever they gauge that I'm ready, then I'll accept that. In the meantime, I'm just gonna keep working my butt off."
More Red Sox Coverage
Crochet's work on Tuesday involved 16 pitches, and he estimated he was sitting at 94-96 mph on his fastball velocity. The left-hander said how well he recovers on Wednesday will be a significant determinant on his ability to pitch in games. Yet when asked if he'll pitch in a regular-season game this weekend or save his return for the postseason, he is leaving that decision to chief baseball officer Craig Breslow and manager Chad Tracy.
"I think that I'm just gonna do whatever they tell me to do, to be honest," he said. "I think that [live BPs] and games, obviously it's a big step up and the pressure of the moment, I suppose, and the intensity. But I don't think that there's a set amount of [live BPs] that need to be thrown before a game."
Tracy, who officially dropped the interim tag earlier in the day, said that whatever decision is made on Crochet, it will be "done with Garrett's best interests in mind."
"Looking at what is he able to accomplish this week, and what does the playoffs require?" Tracy explained. "And then deciding can he fit that role or not based on what he's done."
Ceddanne Rafaela
Rafaela, who hasn't played since Sept. 2 due to a hamstring injury, partook in the live BP with Crochet as he nears a return to the lineup.
"Much better," Tracy said on Rafaela. "Getting close there."
Rafaela has produced the best offensive season of his career, as he's batted .282 with a .760 OPS in 135 games, while continuing to provide Gold Glove-level defense in center field.
Willson Contreras
Tracy also shared a positive injury update on Willson Contreras, who continues to improve after taking a pitch off his right hand last Thursday.
Tracy said that Contreras is "doing much better" and is "swinging aggressively" as he works his way back to full strength.
Aroldis Chapman
Closer Aroldis Chapman hasn't pitched since Sept. 13 due to some lat tightness, but Tracy had yet another positive injury update.
"He's getting very close," Tracy said. "I think we're a day or two away from him being ready to roll."
Group staying ready in Fort Myers
The Red Sox are keeping a team of reinforcements ready in Fort Myers for the playoff run, in case anybody is needed as an injury replacement along the way. That list of players includes:
- SP Tanner Houck
- SP Johan Oviedo
- SS/2B Franklin Arias
- OF Braiden Ward
- RP Wyatt Olds
- SS/2B Tsung-Che Cheng
- RP Tyler Samaniego
- 1B/2B Romy Gonzalez
- RP Jedixson Paez
Curtis Mead
Perhaps the lone negative injury update from Tracy was on second baseman Curtis Mead, who broke his wrist in his first game with the Red Sox on July 27.
"Haven't ruled it out yet. It's gonna be tough," Tracy said when asked if Mead might be able to return for the first round of the playoffs.
Tracy said that Mead is taking some overhand batting practice, but there may not be enough time for Mead to progress to being game-ready.
"I said we would probably be a little aggressive to see how the hand responds," Tracy said. "Have not ruled it out. It's just we're getting up against it a bit."

item.title: [bosoxinjection.com] Red Sox just buried a Craig Breslow show of faith in Chad Tracy news drop
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: After a rollercoaster of a season which included a brutal start, sudden managerial firings, historic win streaks and a playoff clinch, the Boston Red Sox have extended the man who brought it all together. Boston has removed Chad Tracy's "interim" tag and made him their manager, first reported by Christopher Smith of MassLive. Tracy and the Red Sox have agreed to a three-year contract with a club option in 2030, per Smith. His salary has not yet been reported. Tracy was Boston's Triple-A manager
item.content:encoded:
After a rollercoaster of a season which included a brutal start, sudden managerial firings, historic win streaks and a playoff clinch, the Boston Red Sox have extended the man who brought it all together. Boston has removed Chad Tracy's "interim" tag and made him their manager, first reported by Christopher Smith of MassLive.
Tracy and the Red Sox have agreed to a three-year contract with a club option in 2030, per Smith. His salary has not yet been reported.
Tracy was Boston's Triple-A manager on April 25, the day Alex Cora and six other members of his coaching staff were fired. The Red Sox then flew him out to Baltimore to take over in a whirlwind and a leap of faith, and it worked. He'll be the 49th manager in Red Sox franchise history (subscription required).
The Red Sox had a 10-17 record on the day of Tracy's promotion and he managed the club to two games below .500 by July 12, the start of the All-Star break. Boston's historic 15-game winning streak had already begun by then — it rallied to sweep the New York Yankees in four games two weeks before, lost a series to the Washington Nationals, and it was all winning from there.
Red Sox name Chad Tracy manager through 2029, exercised club options to keep Craig Breslow CBO through 2030
Tracy had long been revered as the manager of the WooSox and it didn't take long for Red Sox fans to become equally endeared to him. His direct, but friendly communication style offered a stark contrast to other leaders in the organization. He had preexisting relationships with many of the organization's young players from their time in Triple-A and from rehab assignments, and it showed. After the Red Sox's historic July and August spell, Tracy's promotion seemed almost inevitable, and rightfully so.
Within the Tracy contract announcement, the Red Sox also included another contract update. The Red Sox have exercised the 2029-30 club options on Craig Breslow's contract, essentially extending him for another two years.
This is quite a sign of trust from Boston. Breslow's tenure started with some massive moves like the Garrett Crochet trade, and the Red Sox made the playoffs for the first time in three seasons with him at the helm. But his communication style has been criticized, it's led to massive trades of players who were supposed to be fixtiures of the organization for years to come, and front office leaks have marred his public image.
But Breslow has loosened up a bit since the beginning of the season. He's been pictured around the players more often and has been cracking jokes on his radio appearances.
There's also no denying that he had a great 2025-26 offseason. Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Ranger Suarez and Caleb Durbin, all acquired by Breslow over the offseason, are all major parts of the Red Sox's success.
Cora had been Boston's manager for eight seasons and many Red Sox fans couldn't stand Breslow at the beginning of June. Things can change quickly in baseball.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Red Sox Get Ceddanne Rafaela Update Ahead of Guardians Series
item.dc:creator: Keith Watkins
item.description: The Boston Red Sox have scored 2.82 runs per game across their last 11 outings. The lineup is collectively batting .210 and posting a .621 OPS in that span. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have scored 2.82 runs per game across their last 11 outings. The lineup is collectively batting .210 and posting a .621 OPS in that span. Wilyer Abreu, Adley Rutschman, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, and Nick Sogard have all gone cold at the wrong time.
With the Wild Card Series beginning September 29, the Red Sox need their bats to wake up before October arrives.
The cavalry is coming. And the timing could not be better.
The Latest on Rafaela
Ceddanne Rafaela is expected to return to the lineup on Tuesday when the Red Sox open a three-game series against the Guardians at Fenway Park.
The All-Star center fielder has been sidelined for 16 games since straining his right quadriceps.
Chad Tracy indicated over the weekend that Rafaela should come off the injured list for the homestand. The rotation is set up with Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suarez, a sequence that mirrors how the staff could be deployed in the Wild Card Series.
Getting Rafaela back before those games begin gives him a chance to find his timing and reintegrate into the lineup before the stakes get higher.
What Rafaela Brings Back
Rafaela's absence has been felt. On the season, he has produced 16 home runs, 70 RBIs, and a .282/.760 line. His combination of contact, power, and speed makes him one of the most complete players on the roster.
The defensive impact is equally significant. Rafaela's range in center field changes the way the pitching staff operates. Fly balls that fall for hits with other outfielders become outs when he is patrolling the middle of the outfield. His presence there tightens the entire defense.
The Red Sox have been using Jarren Duran and Nate Eaton to fill the void in center. Both have been serviceable, but neither provides the combination of offense and defense that Rafaela delivers on a daily basis.
The Red Sox Offense Needs a Spark
The numbers paint a clear picture of how badly the Red Sox have struggled at the plate.
Mickey Gasper is 4-for-25 over the recent stretch. Kiner-Falefa has managed just one hit in his last 20 at-bats. Sogard is 8-for-40. The lineup has lacked the consistent production that fueled the summer surge.
There have been bright spots. Roman Anthony broke out of a prolonged slump with a 5-for-13 weekend against the Rays that included two doubles and a homer. Trevor Story has been one of the hottest hitters on the roster since returning from the injured list, carrying a .338 average with an .869 OPS across 19 games.
Willson Contreras is also working his way back from a bruised right hand and could return this week. If both Contreras and Rafaela rejoin the lineup for the Guardians series, it would be the healthiest the Red Sox' batting order has looked in weeks.
Final Word for the Red Sox
The Red Sox have six games left before the playoffs begin.
Rafaela's return gives the lineup a jolt it needs. What he provides on both sides of the ball is invaluable for Boston.
Fenway awaits.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Red Sox Get Ceddanne Rafaela Update Ahead of Guardians Series appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [nesn.com] Chad Tracy Delivers Powerful Message After Red Sox Clinch Playoff Spot | NESN
item.dc:creator: Rodney Knuppel
item.description: The Boston Red Sox did not clinch their postseason berth with a dramatic walk-off hit or a dominant performance from their pitching staff. They clinched after losing 5-1 to the Tampa Bay Rays and receiving help from Mike Yastrzemski and the Atlanta Braves. Interim manager Chad Tracy did not care how the ticket was punched. “When you work as hard as we have worked, I don’t think you care much how it gets done,” Tracy told reporters. “You just want to see your ticket get punched.” That message per
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox did not clinch their postseason berth with a dramatic walk-off hit or a dominant performance from their pitching staff. They clinched after losing 5-1 to the Tampa Bay Rays and receiving help from Mike Yastrzemski and the Atlanta Braves.
Interim manager Chad Tracy did not care how the ticket was punched.
“When you work as hard as we have worked, I don’t think you care much how it gets done,” Tracy told reporters. “You just want to see your ticket get punched.”
That message perfectly captured Boston’s remarkable season. The Red Sox were 32-46 and appeared destined to spend the summer discussing trades, organizational changes and another disappointing finish. Instead, they became the first team in MLB history to finish above .500 and reach the playoffs after losing at least 46 of its first 78 games.
“They didn’t take no for an answer,” Tracy said.
Where It Started
Tracy inherited a 10-17 team when the Red Sox moved on from Alex Cora in April. There was no immediate transformation, and Boston’s season continued to drift for several weeks.
Eventually, everything changed. Boston swept four games from the New York Yankees at Fenway Park in late June and began one of the most impressive turnarounds in franchise history. Young players developed into meaningful contributors, the clubhouse remained together and the Red Sox kept finding ways to survive injuries.
The result is a second consecutive postseason appearance and another likely Wild Card Series against the Yankees. That matchup did not work out for Boston last October. The Red Sox won the opener behind Garrett Crochet but dropped the next two games in New York.
This year’s roster has traveled a much different road.
The Red Sox have played meaningful baseball for months because almost every loss threatened to undo the progress they had made. Players such as Roman Anthony, Payton Tolle and Connelly Early have grown up in that environment, while veterans including Trevor Story and Willson Contreras helped keep the clubhouse steady.
Getting Things Set Up
Now Boston has an opportunity to set its rotation, protect tired relievers and enter the postseason with more than a week to prepare. The final regular-season games still matter, especially with the Cleveland Guardians visiting Fenway Park. Boston can use the series to evaluate potential postseason matchups and determine which pitchers are best equipped for important October innings.
The celebration also strengthens Tracy’s case to remain manager beyond this season. Boston did not merely improve after he took control. The Red Sox completed a turnaround that had never been accomplished in major league history.
Tracy did not want credit Sunday. His message remained focused on the players who refused to allow a terrible start to define them. That approach may be one of the biggest reasons the Red Sox are still playing.

item.title: [mlb.com] Our final MVP poll has clear frontrunners, but can this week change anything?
item.dc:creator: Brian Murphy
item.description: As we make our way through the final week of the regular season, there doesn't seem to be much suspense as to who will be named MVP. item.content:encoded:
As we make our way through the final week of the regular season, there doesn't seem to be much suspense as to who will be named MVP. At least, that's what we can glean from our latest -- and final -- MLB.com 2026 MVP poll.
Yordan Alvarez is still well out in front in the American League despite relatively mediocre production of late. In the National League, Pete Crow-Armstrong is wrapping up one of the best all-around seasons in recent memory.
Thirty-eight MLB.com experts cast votes for who they think will earn MVP honors after this season, with 32 players receiving at least one vote. As a reminder, votes were based not only on results so far, but also on how things are expected to play out the rest of the season.
Voters ranked their top five picks in each league on a 5-4-3-2-1 scale -- five points for a first-place vote, four points for a second-place vote and so on. Here are the results.
All stats are through Sunday unless otherwise noted.
AMERICAN LEAGUE
Alvarez has been so good this year that what qualifies as a slump for him would be a good stretch for most other hitters. Over his past 41 games, he is hitting .264 with an .840 OPS. Again, not bad for most, but well below the standard of the AL leader in average (.313) and OPS (1.027). Alvarez has three homers and five RBIs through 16 games this month, leaving him tied with the O's Pete Alonso and one home run behind the Rays' Junior Caminero for the AL lead and nine RBIs behind Alonso for the top spot in that statistic. Even though his Triple Crown chances have faded, Alvarez has still put together an awesome 2026 at the plate. His 179 wRC+ is at least 27 points better than any other qualified hitter.
We know Caminero is one of the game's great sluggers. He is finishing up his second straight 40-homer season and swings harder than anyone. But what's been most impressive about his season is his improved strike-zone judgment. He has upped his walk rate from a below-average 6.3% to 11.5%, which ranks in the 80th percentile of MLB. He's also maintained a very solid strikeout rate (18.5%). He's not chasing as much, has shaved his whiff rate and is making more contact overall. That blend of patience, power and bat control is a special combination, especially in a 23-year-old player. Carrying a .363 on-base percentage (52 points better than last season), Caminero's .892 OPS ranks third in the AL.
Witt has had better offensive seasons, although 18 homers, 43 steals and a 119 wRC+ in 137 games is not too shabby. But when you consider his entire skill set, Witt remains extremely valuable. His +16 fielding run value is tied for third in the Majors, and his 22 outs above average tops the AL. He also has a +8 baserunning run value, one behind the D-backs' Corbin Carroll for the MLB lead. So while he hasn't been as undeniable in the batter's box as he was in 2024 (169 wRC+), Witt's all-around greatness has him atop the AL FanGraphs WAR leaderboard (6.6) and in line for a possible top-five finish in the MVP voting for the third time in three years.
There has been quite a bit of MVP chatter surrounding Schlittler in recent weeks. And why not? He is pacing the AL in ERA (1.94), WHIP (0.91) and FanGraphs pitching WAR (6.1). He ranks second in the junior circuit in opponents' batting average (.182) and strikeout-minus-walk rate (25.0%). He has allowed one or zero runs in 21 starts. That's a Yankees franchise record and something only two other pitchers age-25 or younger have accomplished in the Live Ball Era (since 1920): Blake Snell (2018) and Dean Chance (1964). He seems like a lock for the AL Cy Young Award at this point, but Schlittler will receive his fair share of MVP love.
Schlittler hasn't been the only indispensable Yankee this year. While New York has been without Aaron Judge for a large portion of the season and has missed other star bats as well due to injuries, Rice has been a constant. He ranks third in the AL in homers (39) and runs scored (100). He's fourth in the league in RBIs (95) and OPS (.888), and tied for fourth in batting run value (+34). With two homers during the final week, Rice would become just the second non-Judge Yankee over the past decade to hit at least 41 homers in a season, joining Juan Soto (2024).
Others receiving votes: Willson Contreras, Red Sox; Pete Alonso, Orioles; Kevin McGonigle, Tigers; Miguel Vargas, White Sox; Randy Arozarena, Mariners; Munetaka Murakami, White Sox; Dylan Cease, Blue Jays
NATIONAL LEAGUE
Last month, PCA jumped over Ohtani and into the No. 1 spot in our poll. This month, he has run away from the rest of the field. The recipient of every first-place vote cast by our panel, Crow-Armstrong is tied with Kyle Schwarber for the MLB lead in home runs (45). No one has more runs (118), extra-base hits (83) or total bases (351) this season. With 38 steals, the Cubs' dynamic center fielder could become the seventh member of the 40-40 club later this week. Oh, and let's not overlook the fact that he is arguably the best defensive player at any position right now. It's no longer a question of whether Crow-Armstrong is the NL MVP. The award is as good as his right now. But will he win it in unanimous fashion?
Ohtani remains the clear runner-up in the NL despite playing in just three games this month due to his nagging left knee and right biceps injuries. The good news is Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said "there's a good chance" Ohtani will be activated from the 15-day injured list Wednesday after a minimum stint. He won't pitch for the rest of the season, leaving him with a 1.79 ERA and 95 K's over 85 2/3 innings. But Ohtani will have a few games to add to his offensive totals (30 homers, 142 wRC+).
We mentioned earlier how Schlittler looks like the heavy favorite for the AL Cy Young Award. Misiorowski is an even bigger shoo-in in the senior circuit. Through 169 1/3 innings, Miz leads the Majors in just about every category, including ERA (1.86), WHIP (0.80), strikeout-minus-walk rate (31.7%) and fWAR (6.5), to name just a few. Opposing batters have a scant .474 OPS against Misiorowski, which is the second-lowest by any qualified starter in the Divisional Era (since 1969). Pedro Martinez, in one of the greatest seasons by a pitcher, recorded a .473 opponents' OPS in 2000.
De La Cruz, who didn't receive a single vote in our previous MVP poll, has been red-hot for Cincinnati over the past month. In his last 27 games, he is batting .404 with eight homers, six steals and a 1.205 OPS. He collected multiple hits in 14 of those games, and his 2.5 fWAR during this period is the best in the big leagues. This prolonged hot streak has given De La Cruz a career-best 139 wRC+ and has left him two homers and two steals away from becoming the fourth Red in the 30-30 club and the first since Brandon Phillips in 2007.
Schwarber has fallen into a bit of a rut, going 4-for-34 with one home run over his past 10 games. He's also eight strikeouts away from setting a new record for K's in a single season. Even so, you have to admire Schwarber's consistency. He will end up with more than 40 homers and 150 games played in four of the past five seasons. He has surpassed 100 walks for a fourth consecutive season, and a third NL home run title is right there for the taking, too.
Others receiving votes: Fernando Tatis Jr., Padres; Brice Turang, Brewers; Matt Olson, Braves; James Wood, Nationals; Jordan Walker, Cardinals; Alex Bregman, Cubs; Bryce Harper, Phillies; Jake Bauers, Brewers; Otto Lopez, Marlins; Gabriel Moreno, Diamondbacks; Rafael Devers, Giants; Alec Burleson, Cardinals; CJ Abrams, Nationals; Corbin Carroll, Diamondbacks; Cristopher Sánchez, Phillies

item.title: [El ExtraBase] Willson Contreras: "Nunca dejamos de trabajar por ese cupo a los playoffs" - El ExtraBase
item.dc:creator: Elextrabase
